g7_warnings.warning: The paper obtains four months of 2019-2020 fire data but calculates only two without a predeclared selection rule, archived input table, exclusion ledger, coordinate reference system, or transformation code.

Predictable fires, ignorable malicious ignition, perfectly reliable equipment, accurate research data, and personnel near possible fires are asserted as premises; they remove important failure modes rather than validating the deployment system.

Equation (2) is one unnormalized isotropic Gaussian-shaped expression with no mixture weights, component covariance matrices, fitted component count, likelihood, training procedure, or held-out evaluation, so it does not specify the claimed Gaussian mixture model.

Equation (3) visually places fire frequency in a denominator although the narrative treats higher frequency as increasing deployment, while Equation (4) uses f as a summation bound; k, A, P, f, and personnel integrality are not identified consistently.

Euclidean coordinate distance and SSE do not enforce 30 km coverage, construction-cost tradeoffs, capacity, terrain, roads, or outlier service; K is called proper but no selection rule, initialization, seed, scaling, or convergence trace is supplied.

Minimizing total channel length does not by itself minimize repeater count under terrain-dependent ranges; Equations (9)-(10) have ambiguous endpoint addition, segment indexing, topology, integer placement, and line-of-sight semantics.

Table 2 labels A$50 as drone cost, Equations (11) and (19) assert A$10,000 construction plus maintenance, and the budget later uses A$10,000 plus A$50; the Sony battery search citation does not establish EOC, aircraft, repeater, or lifecycle prices.

The derivation initially excludes charging, then doubles a group for a perfect recharge handoff without endurance, charge duration, route closure, launch timing, integer rounding, collision avoidance, or a schedulable timeline; N_SSA,1/2 is visually and semantically ambiguous.

Equations (16)-(18) set the unmonitored interval to zero and one half-group aircraft per fire point without defining alternating relief, observation footprint, charging, failure, or why the strategy dominates when the strategy-A count exceeds the number of points.

Equation (20) omits the normalization formulas and directions, uses the uncovered share in both safety and observation, assumes communication is already 100%, and adds quantities whose uncertainty and measurement roles are not reconciled.

Equation (20) defines alpha, beta, gamma, delta in capability-safety-economics-observation order, but the reported vector is described in safety-capability-economics-observation order; the first two coefficients therefore drift unless an unstated remapping occurred.

The reported 73 repeaters plus 80 SSA in November and 80 repeaters plus 104 SSA in December are visible results, but no frozen data, K choice, GMM fit, MST edges, cruise tolerance, feasible alternatives, solver objective, or optimality certificate is supplied.

Equation (23) uses accumulated x^(1)(k) rather than a defined neighboring background value, normal equations are printed without conditioning or residual tests, and ten annual observations are extrapolated for another ten years without forecast intervals or held-out checks.

Temperature and precipitation alone are treated as fire likelihood, and 26.93 C plus 401.81 mm in 2030 is called the worst condition without uncertainty, station representativeness, fuel, wind, ignition, seasonality, or a calibrated fire-occurrence measurement model.

Each named type changes multiple undeclared factors such as probability thresholds, location concentration, fire size, frequency, personnel dispersion, EOC demand, and communication geometry; the three composite scenarios cannot support single-factor causal cost language.

The A$1,506,000, A$1,206,500, and A$1,095,950 increments reconcile arithmetically, but matching qualitative expectations is not external validation and the closest-to-2030 survey data, scenario configurations, baseline files, and replay outputs are absent.

The model changes a planar range circle to a sphere and states that signals cannot cross mountains, but supplies no 3D distance equation, radio link budget, obstruction/line-of-sight algorithm, coordinate list, objective values, feasible masks, or measured terrain-channel validation.

One-at-a-time deterministic changes in k, N_EOC, and t do not test data, seed, clustering, structure, terrain, or scenario robustness; N_EOC is also a decision variable, k and fire size are not interchangeable across downstream clustering, and interactions and threshold movement are omitted.

Eight EOCs at A$50,000 plus 184 drones at A$10,050 and A$250,000 other equipment sum to A$2,499,200, supporting only an approximate A$2.5 million arithmetic request; quotations, taxes, staffing, batteries, operations, replacement, contingency, and uncertainty are not itemized.

Several web URLs are not passage-level archived sources, the BOM link is not shown to represent the modeled region, and no code, environment, random seeds, raw monthly fire records, terrain grid, fitted parameters, intermediate outputs, or end-to-end replay package is supplied.
